newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 10.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - A round of replenishment purchases after the holidays got 1997 trading off to a solid start, Random Lengths said in its weekly cash market review. Activity tailed off toward the end of the week in Canadian items but remained solid in other species, notably Southern Pine and green Douglas fir.

Traders blamed a downturn in futures for the slower pace in S-P-F and nasty weather in parts of the Midwest and East further cooled enthusiasm on Thursday. But prices finished higher on most framing items. The need to refill gaps in dealer and distributor inventories generated most of the week's activity. Yet fear of a market correction kept a rein on buyers.

Wholesalers were cautiously optimistic early in the week and did some buying, Random Lengths said. But a number of them turned more bearish from Wednesday onward and focused on selling what they owned, often at less than mills were asking. Producers kept a positive outlook, pointing to late Jan shipping times.
Some buyers, however, countered that purchases since the holidays had covered needs through early February.

A number of producers had less-than-normal volumes to offer, for a variety of reasons. Some cited production lost during holiday shutdowns. Mills along the West Coast from California to British Columbia wrestled with logging, production and shipping problems stemming from recent storms, Random Lengths said. A few manufacturers in California remained shut down due to flooding.
Rumors circulated that Canada shipments last quarter had been understated due to a large backlog of unprocessed export permits. But Canadian authorities said there was no big backlog.
Canadian exports as of Dec 31 were at 83.7 percent of Oct-Dec quota and 80.9 pct of annual April/March quota, it said.
